    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4754:## 4. Receive the configuration in `UART_CLK`
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4756:In the UART clock domain:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4761:- Wait one or two extra `UART_CLK` cycles.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4762:- Capture the synchronized bus into `cfg_uart`.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4770:reg [15:0] cfg_uart;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4774:always @(posedge UART_CLK or negedge uart_rst) begin
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4775:    if (!uart_rst) begin
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4779:        cfg_uart      <= 16'h2081; // match reset configuration
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4795:            cfg_uart     <= cfg_bus_sync2;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4813:Instead, drive it from a registered UART-domain configuration:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4816:wire [7:0] tx_div_cfg = cfg_uart[15:8];
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4817:wire [5:0] prescale_cfg = cfg_uart[7:2];
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4837:because changing `is_valid` or `i_div_ratio` while the clock is active can create a malformed clock pulse. For UART operation, it is safest to require a divider ratio of at least 2 and avoid runtime bypass switching entirely.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4841:`cfg_uart` is stable in the `UART_CLK` domain, but TX uses `tx_clk` and RX uses `rx_clk`.

    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4859:If this is a fixed-configuration UART after reset, you can use a simpler policy:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4861:- Program `reg2` and `reg3` only while reset is asserted or before UART traffic starts.

    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4872:what if these configuartions never change , or only changed once at the start then is left as is later , almost like a quastiStatic
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4886:For your UART, I would recommend option 2 if you genuinely need to change settings once.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4901:## Option 2: configure once, then start UART
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4909:4. Transfer the stable configuration into UART_CLK.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4910:5. Program the UART clock dividers from that stable copy.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4916:The important part is: `reg2`/`reg3` must be stable before the UART becomes active.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4918:A compact implementation is to add `uart_enable` or `cfg_done`.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4921:wire uart_enable;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4927:- UART does not transmit or receive.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4929:- A UART-clock-domain copy captures the config.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4931:Then assert `uart_enable` once configuration has settled.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4933:For example, use a `UART_CLK` register to capture configuration:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4936:reg [7:0] reg2_uart;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4937:reg [7:0] reg3_uart;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4939:always @(posedge UART_CLK or negedge uart_rst) begin
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4940:    if (!uart_rst) begin
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4941:        reg2_uart <= 8'h81;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4942:        reg3_uart <= 8'h20;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4944:    else if (!uart_enable) begin
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4945:        reg2_uart <= reg2;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4946:        reg3_uart <= reg3;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4951:This is acceptable only if the source registers are guaranteed not to change while `uart_enable == 0`, and they remain stable for several `UART_CLK` cycles before you set `uart_enable`.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4953:Then use the UART-domain copies for the dividers:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4956:.i_div_ratio(reg3_uart)
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4959:and derive RX divider configuration from `reg2_uart`, not directly from `reg2`.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4961:After `uart_enable` becomes `1`, lock the values:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4965:    reg2_uart <= reg2_uart;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4966:    reg3_uart <= reg3_uart;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4973:wire tx_rst_int = tx_rst & uart_enable;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4974:wire rx_rst_int = rx_rst & uart_enable;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4980:wire tx_rst_int = tx_rst & uart_enable;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4983:This needs care: when `uart_enable = 0`, the resulting reset becomes low and keeps logic reset. When it becomes `1`, `tx_rst`/`rx_rst` must already have been synchronized.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4988:assign tx_rst_int = uart_enable ? tx_rst : 1'b0;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4989:assign rx_rst_int = uart_enable ? rx_rst : 1'b0;
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:4996:Do not configure through UART commands “at startup” unless the UART already has known default divider/prescale settings that permit those commands to be received. In your design, `reg2` and `reg3` reset defaults provide this bootstrap configuration.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:5001:Reset defaults boot the UART.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:5027:I’ll set the configuration CDC aside as requested and do a final pass for independent compile, synthesis, reset, FIFO, and UART functional issues in the current files.

    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:5320:Lint reports missing pins for `parity_error` and `framing_error` at the UART top-level instance. This is not functionally wrong if you do not use them, but connect them to unused wires to keep lint clean:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:5337:- The system always sends an ALU response as two UART bytes.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:5427:An attempted `0xAA` write to address `0` or `1` will simply be ignored. If your protocol needs explicit error reporting, you could later add a UART error response, but silently ignoring protected writes is reasonable for now.

    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6232:At a high level, the system is a UART-controlled register-file/ALU system. You send command bytes serially into `RX_IN`; it interprets them in `SYS_CTRL`; some commands change registers or run the ALU; any response is queued in the asynchronous FIFO and serially transmitted on `TX_OUT`.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6238:UART RX ──► Data_Sync ──► SYS_CTRL ──► Register file / ALU
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6248:                              UART TX ──► TX_OUT
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6260:reg2 = 0x81   UART configuration
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6273:While idle, `TX_OUT` remains high, which is normal UART idle behavior.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6277:The UART RX block receives one serial frame from `RX_IN`:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6317:writes `0x81` into register 2, which changes the UART configuration.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6324:address 2 → UART prescale/parity configuration
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6344:causes the register file to read `reg2`, then `SYS_CTRL` puts that one byte into the FIFO. UART TX eventually transmits that byte.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6375:  → UART transmits 08, then 00
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6448:The controller works in the `REF_CLK` domain, while UART TX works at `tx_clk`. The FIFO safely bridges them.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6456:  → UART TX starts transmission
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6462:If multiple response bytes are queued, UART TX continues sending them in order.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6476:2. Read default UART configuration:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6502:In every case, remember that UART bytes are physically serialized with start/parity/stop bits on `TX_OUT`; the values above are logical byte values, not the raw bit waveform.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6510:You must send a complete UART frame on `RX_IN`, not just drive the 8-bit byte value.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6538:Your testbench should drive `RX_IN` at the UART bit period, not assign `RX_IN = 8'hCC`. The UART RX module will reconstruct `0xCC` internally and assert `RX_OUT_V`.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6542:Sequence of Operation (Must include in the testbench): -
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6549:It means that after reset, your testbench should first configure the UART-related registers using the normal register-write command (`0xAA`).
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6558:Each value is a UART byte frame on `RX_IN`, not a parallel 8-bit assignment.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6567:writes UART RX/parity configuration into `reg2`.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6613:Only after that should the testbench send functional commands such as:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6621:One practical detail: if you change `reg2` prescale or parity settings, your testbench must immediately start sending later UART frames using the new RX timing/parity configuration. If you change `reg3`, the UART output baud timing changes, so the testbench’s TX monitor must decode `TX_OUT` using the new divider ratio.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6634:        @(negedge UART_CLK);
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6637:            @(negedge UART_CLK);
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6640:        @(negedge UART_CLK);
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6642:        @(negedge UART_CLK);
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6649:Not as intended for your UART receiver.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6651:The main issue is timing: your task holds each bit for only one `UART_CLK` cycle:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6654:@(negedge UART_CLK);
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6657:But RX expects each UART bit to remain stable for `Prescale` cycles of `rx_clk`. With the reset configuration, `Prescale = 32`, so one UART frame bit must remain stable for 32 `rx_clk` cycles—not one `UART_CLK` cycle.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6684:        // Data bits: UART is LSB-first
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6723:If you later change the UART prescale, replace the fixed `32` with a testbench variable such as `rx_prescale`, and update it after sending the configuration command.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:6725:Your `start_bit` and `stop_bit` task inputs are unnecessary: UART start is always `0`, stop is always `1`.

    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7557:So yes: a normal write can accidentally overwrite `reg2` or `reg3`, changing UART behavior.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7575:0x2, 0x3  → UART configuration; only initialization may write them
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7602:            WrEn = 1'b1; // Initial UART configuration only
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7645:But if you want to change UART configuration during operation, a permanent lock is not the best architecture.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7678:- Changing `reg3` while UART TX is transmitting can corrupt the current TX frame by changing its bit timing.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7679:- Changing `reg2` prescale/parity while UART RX is receiving can corrupt the current RX frame.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7680:- If the host changes its UART settings before the DUT changes its settings, subsequent command bytes can be decoded incorrectly.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7685:- Send configuration frames using the old UART settings.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7689:- Switch the testbench/host UART settings only after that point.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7695:- If configuration can change later: add a dedicated configuration command such as `0xEE`, block `0xAA` writes to `0x0–0x3`, and apply configuration only while UART is idle.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7957:This allows only addresses `0x4–0xF` while unlocked. It never permits `0x2` or `0x3`, so initialization cannot configure UART registers.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:7996:        // UART configuration locations: allowed only during initialization

    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8562:Your testbench is a good smoke test, but it is not sufficient to reliably identify problems yet. It drives most major commands, but it has no automatic checks and currently does not verify the serial `TX_OUT` result end-to-end.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8592:- Your `wave.do` UART hierarchy paths are old:
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8595:/tb/DUT/UART_TX_RX/...
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8601:/tb/DUT/U1/U0_UART_RX/P_DATA
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8602:/tb/DUT/U1/U0_UART_RX/Data_Valid
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8603:/tb/DUT/U1/U0_UART_TX/P_DATA
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8604:/tb/DUT/U1/U0_UART_TX/Data_Valid
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8613:ModelSim silently skips invalid wave paths. So you may not actually be observing TX/RX UART internals.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8673:The strongest next improvement is a UART TX monitor task that decodes `TX_OUT` and compares these expected bytes automatically. Until then, this testbench confirms internal activity, but not that the final serial output is correct.
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8677:you can modify the tb to make more test cases as you see fit wit auto checking
    ./rtl/codex-session-01a0bb84-59a7-7483-be7e-87352c4f57b4zoz.md:8681:I’m upgrading it into a self-checking end-to-end test: it will verify register protections directly and decode/compare UART TX response bytes automatically.

    module tb;
        localparam int WIDTH=8, ALU_OUT_WIDTH=16, RF_DEPTH=16, RF_ADDR_WIDTH=4;
        localparam int FUN_WIDTH=4, FIFO_DEPTH=8, FIFO_ADDR_WIDTH=3, PTR_SIZE=4;
        localparam time REF_HALF_PERIOD=5ns, UART_HALF_PERIOD=135.6335ns;
    
        integer rx_prescale=32;
        integer error_count=0;
        logic REF_CLK, UART_CLK, RST, RX_IN, TX_OUT;
    
        sys_top #(.WIDTH(WIDTH), .ALU_OUT_WIDTH(ALU_OUT_WIDTH), .RF_DEPTH(RF_DEPTH),
                  .RF_ADDR_WIDTH(RF_ADDR_WIDTH), .FUN_WIDTH(FUN_WIDTH),
                  .FIFO_DEPTH(FIFO_DEPTH), .FIFO_ADDR_WIDTH(FIFO_ADDR_WIDTH),
                  .PTR_SIZE(PTR_SIZE)) DUT (
            .REF_CLK(REF_CLK), .UART_CLK(UART_CLK), .RST(RST),
            .RX_IN(RX_IN), .TX_OUT(TX_OUT)
        );
    
        always #REF_HALF_PERIOD REF_CLK=~REF_CLK;
        always #UART_HALF_PERIOD UART_CLK=~UART_CLK;
    
        task automatic check_equal8(input string name, input logic [7:0] actual,
                                    input logic [7:0] expected);
            begin
                if (actual !== expected) begin
                    error_count=error_count+1;
                    $error("%s: expected 0x%02h, got 0x%02h", name, expected, actual);
                end else $display("PASS: %s = 0x%02h", name, actual);
            end
        endtask
    
        task automatic initialize;
            begin
                REF_CLK=0; UART_CLK=0; RX_IN=1; RST=0;
                repeat (2) @(negedge UART_CLK);
                RST=1;
                // Wait for ref_rst, uart_rst, tx_rst, and rx_rst to release.
                repeat (10) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk);
            end
        endtask
    
        // The configuration used in this test has even parity enabled.
        task automatic send_frame(input logic [7:0] data);
            integer i;
            logic parity_bit;
            begin
                parity_bit=^data;
                RX_IN=0; repeat (rx_prescale) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk); // start
                for (i=0; i<WIDTH; i=i+1) begin
                    RX_IN=data[i];
                    repeat (rx_prescale) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk);
                end
                RX_IN=parity_bit; repeat (rx_prescale) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk);
                RX_IN=1;          repeat (rx_prescale) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk); // stop
            end
        endtask
    
        task automatic send_write(input logic [3:0] address, input logic [7:0] data);
            begin
                send_frame(8'hAA); send_frame({4'h0,address}); send_frame(data);
                repeat (8) @(posedge REF_CLK);
            end
        endtask
    
        task automatic send_read(input logic [3:0] address);
            begin send_frame(8'hBB); send_frame({4'h0,address}); end
        endtask
    
        task automatic send_alu_new(input logic [7:0] a, input logic [7:0] b,
                                    input logic [3:0] func);
            begin
                send_frame(8'hCC); send_frame(a); send_frame(b); send_frame({4'h0,func});
            end
        endtask
    
        task automatic send_alu_stored(input logic [3:0] func);
            begin send_frame(8'hDD); send_frame({4'h0,func}); end
        endtask
    
        // Decodes one entire UART TX frame.  TX data changes on tx_clk rising

## Assistant

Yes—for functional regression, use the same TB with DFT held inactive.

Your current `tb.sv` omits the new DFT inputs, so they float (`Z`), especially `test_mode`, which can propagate `X` through the clock/reset muxes. Add and drive:

```systemverilog
logic scan_clk, scan_rst, test_mode, SE;
logic [2:0] SI, SO;

sys_top #(...) DUT (
  .REF_CLK(REF_CLK), .UART_CLK(UART_CLK), .RST(RST),
  .RX_IN(RX_IN), .TX_OUT(TX_OUT),
  .scan_clk(scan_clk), .scan_rst(scan_rst),
  .test_mode(test_mode), .SE(SE), .SI(SI), .SO(SO)
);

initial begin
  scan_clk  = 0;
  scan_rst  = 0;   // active-low according to the DFT script
  test_mode = 0;   // functional mode
  SE        = 0;   // disable scan shifting
  SI        = '0;
end
```

That works because the DFT wrapper selects the original clocks/resets when `test_mode=0` in [SYS_TOP_dft.v](/home/zeyad/Digital_Diploma_Temsah/UART_System/rtl/System_Top/SYS_TOP_dft.v:26).

For scan-chain validation, though, this TB is not enough: make a separate scan TB that sets `test_mode=1`, pulses `scan_clk`, enables `SE`, shifts `SI`, and checks `SO`.

## Assistant

The first concrete failure is confirmed: the TB leaves every new DFT port unconnected. I’m now running the functional sequence with those pins tied to functional mode, so we can separate that wiring issue from any RTL behavior issue.

## Activity

    file changes: Completed · 1 changes
    Add: /tmp/tb_dft_functional.sv
    `timescale 1ns/1ps
    module tb_dft_functional;
        localparam int WIDTH=8, ALU_OUT_WIDTH=16, RF_DEPTH=16, RF_ADDR_WIDTH=4;
        localparam int FUN_WIDTH=4, FIFO_DEPTH=8, FIFO_ADDR_WIDTH=3, PTR_SIZE=4;
        localparam time REF_HALF_PERIOD=5ns, UART_HALF_PERIOD=135.6335ns;
    
        integer rx_prescale=32;
        integer error_count=0;
        logic REF_CLK, UART_CLK, RST, RX_IN, TX_OUT;
        logic scan_clk, scan_rst, test_mode, SE;
        logic [2:0] SI, SO;
    
        sys_top #(.WIDTH(WIDTH), .ALU_OUT_WIDTH(ALU_OUT_WIDTH), .RF_DEPTH(RF_DEPTH),
                  .RF_ADDR_WIDTH(RF_ADDR_WIDTH), .FUN_WIDTH(FUN_WIDTH),
                  .FIFO_DEPTH(FIFO_DEPTH), .FIFO_ADDR_WIDTH(FIFO_ADDR_WIDTH),
                  .PTR_SIZE(PTR_SIZE)) DUT (
            .REF_CLK(REF_CLK), .UART_CLK(UART_CLK), .RST(RST),
            .RX_IN(RX_IN), .TX_OUT(TX_OUT),
            .scan_clk(scan_clk), .scan_rst(scan_rst), .test_mode(test_mode),
            .SE(SE), .SI(SI), .SO(SO)
        );
    
        always #REF_HALF_PERIOD REF_CLK=~REF_CLK;
        always #UART_HALF_PERIOD UART_CLK=~UART_CLK;
    
        task automatic check_equal8(input string name, input logic [7:0] actual,
                                    input logic [7:0] expected);
            begin
                if (actual !== expected) begin
                    error_count=error_count+1;
                    $error("%s: expected 0x%02h, got 0x%02h", name, expected, actual);
                end else $display("PASS: %s = 0x%02h", name, actual);
            end
        endtask
    
        task automatic initialize;
            begin
                REF_CLK=0; UART_CLK=0; RX_IN=1; RST=0;
                scan_clk=0; scan_rst=0; test_mode=0; SE=0; SI='0;
                repeat (2) @(negedge UART_CLK);
                RST=1;
                repeat (10) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk);
            end
        endtask
    
        task automatic send_frame(input logic [7:0] data);
            integer i;
            logic parity_bit;
            begin
                parity_bit=^data;
                RX_IN=0; repeat (rx_prescale) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk);
                for (i=0; i<WIDTH; i=i+1) begin
                    RX_IN=data[i]; repeat (rx_prescale) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk);
                end
                RX_IN=parity_bit; repeat (rx_prescale) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk);
                RX_IN=1; repeat (rx_prescale) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk);
            end
        endtask
    
        task automatic send_write(input logic [3:0] address, input logic [7:0] data);
            begin send_frame(8'hAA); send_frame({4'h0,address}); send_frame(data); repeat (8) @(posedge REF_CLK); end
        endtask
        task automatic send_read(input logic [3:0] address);
            begin send_frame(8'hBB); send_frame({4'h0,address}); end
        endtask
        task automatic send_alu_new(input logic [7:0] a, input logic [7:0] b, input logic [3:0] func);
            begin send_frame(8'hCC); send_frame(a); send_frame(b); send_frame({4'h0,func}); end
        endtask
        task automatic send_alu_stored(input logic [3:0] func);
            begin send_frame(8'hDD); send_frame({4'h0,func}); end
        endtask
        task automatic expect_tx_byte(input logic [7:0] expected);
            integer i;
            logic [7:0] received;
            logic received_parity;
            begin
                @(negedge TX_OUT); @(negedge DUT.tx_clk); @(negedge DUT.tx_clk); #1ps;
                for (i=0; i<WIDTH; i=i+1) begin
                    received[i]=TX_OUT;
                    if (i<WIDTH-1) begin @(negedge DUT.tx_clk); #1ps; end
                end
                @(negedge DUT.tx_clk); #1ps; received_parity=TX_OUT;
                @(negedge DUT.tx_clk); #1ps;
                if (TX_OUT !== 1'b1) begin error_count=error_count+1; $error("TX stop bit error: got %b", TX_OUT); end
                check_equal8("UART TX byte", received, expected);
                if (received_parity !== (^expected)) begin error_count=error_count+1; $error("TX parity error for 0x%02h", expected); end
            end
        endtask
    
        initial begin
            initialize;
            send_write(4'h2,8'h41); wait (DUT.Regfile_u.REG2 === 8'h41); rx_prescale=16; repeat (2) @(negedge DUT.rx_clk);
            send_write(4'h3,8'h20); wait (DUT.Regfile_u.REG3 === 8'h20); repeat (4) @(posedge REF_CLK);
            check_equal8("reg2 configuration",DUT.Regfile_u.REG2,8'h41); check_equal8("reg3 configuration",DUT.Regfile_u.REG3,8'h20);
            if (DUT.sys_ctrl_u.cfg_locked !== 1'b1) begin error_count=error_count+1; $error("Configuration did not lock"); end
            send_write(4'h5,8'h07); send_write(4'h9,8'h03); check_equal8("reg5 normal write",DUT.Regfile_u.reg_file[5],8'h07); check_equal8("reg9 normal write",DUT.Regfile_u.reg_file[9],8'h03);
            fork expect_tx_byte(8'h07); send_read(4'h5); join
            fork expect_tx_byte(8'h41); send_read(4'h2); join
            fork begin expect_tx_byte(8'h07); expect_tx_byte(8'h00); end send_alu_new(8'd3,8'd4,4'h0); join
            check_equal8("ALU operand A",DUT.Regfile_u.REG0,8'h03); check_equal8("ALU operand B",DUT.Regfile_u.REG1,8'h04);
            fork begin expect_tx_byte(8'h0C); expect_tx_byte(8'h00); end send_alu_stored(4'h2); join
            fork begin expect_tx_byte(8'h32); expect_tx_byte(8'h00); end send_alu_new(8'd100,8'd2,4'h3); join
            send_write(4'h0,8'h99); send_write(4'h1,8'h99); send_write(4'h2,8'h99); send_write(4'h3,8'h99);
            check_equal8("protected reg0",DUT.Regfile_u.REG0,8'h64); check_equal8("protected reg1",DUT.Regfile_u.REG1,8'h02); check_equal8("protected reg2",DUT.Regfile_u.REG2,8'h41); check_equal8("protected reg3",DUT.Regfile_u.REG3,8'h20);
            for (int address=4; address<RF_DEPTH; address++) begin send_write(address[3:0],8'h09); check_equal8("normal register write",DUT.Regfile_u.reg_file[address],8'h09); end
            if (error_count==0) $display("ALL TESTS PASSED"); else $display("TEST FAILED: %0d error(s)", error_count);
            $finish;
        end
    endmodule

## Assistant

Yes. The functional RTL sequence is good once DFT is held in functional mode: I ran the complete TB flow with `test_mode=0`, `SE=0`, and `SI=0`; all checks passed.

The actual issue is in the TB instantiation at [tb.sv](/home/zeyad/Digital_Diploma_Temsah/UART_System/Testbench/tb.sv:14): it does not connect the new DFT pins. In particular, `test_mode` floats as `Z`, while the RTL uses it to mux clocks and resets at [SYS_TOP_dft.v](/home/zeyad/Digital_Diploma_Temsah/UART_System/rtl/System_Top/SYS_TOP_dft.v:26) and [SYS_TOP_dft.v](/home/zeyad/Digital_Diploma_Temsah/UART_System/rtl/System_Top/SYS_TOP_dft.v:82). That can yield `X` clocks/resets and make the TB hang or misbehave.

Add these TB signals and connections:

```systemverilog
logic scan_clk, scan_rst, test_mode, SE;
logic [2:0] SI, SO;

...
.scan_clk(scan_clk),
.scan_rst(scan_rst),
.test_mode(test_mode),
.SE(SE),
.SI(SI),
.SO(SO)
```

Initialize them before releasing functional reset:

```systemverilog
scan_clk  = 0;
scan_rst  = 0;
test_mode = 0;
SE        = 0;
SI        = '0;
```

One important DFT detail: [run.do](/home/zeyad/Digital_Diploma_Temsah/UART_System/run.do:43) compiles `SYS_TOP_dft.v`, not the synthesized inserted-DFT netlist. Also, in that RTL wrapper, `SE` and `SI` are unused and `SO` is undriven—expected only if actual scan-cell insertion happens later in synthesis. So:

- Functional RTL regression: fixed by connecting/tieing off DFT pins.
- Actual scan verification: simulate `System_TOP_NETLIST_DFT.v` with standard-cell models and a scan-specific TB.
